teaser: Container security from the top down: at every layer, keep only the code the layer above needs. Measured on one real tool, with its limits.
core_idea: Bottom-up hardening still leaves code the application never runs, so security should also come from the top: starting from the use case, ask at every layer for the minimum code below and remove the rest; measured on sgit, a use case ran from 428 of 1,500 files while compiled code and coverage blind spots set the limits, and a graph traced from story to build makes the result certifiable.

nodes.label: Bottom up, hardened
nodes.summary: Rebuild the OS and libraries from source, minimal images, a managed process.

nodes.label: Three gaps
nodes.summary: Unused code, assurance by testing, and the loop of granting more when something breaks.

nodes.label: Custom Assembly only adds
nodes.summary: Chainguard's tailoring tool cannot remove the source image's packages by default.

nodes.label: The minimum code below
nodes.summary: At every layer, keep what the layer above needs and remove everything else.

nodes.label: The immutable line
nodes.summary: Draw the line below which nothing changes as high as the evidence allows.

nodes.label: No land to live off
nodes.summary: With only the use case's code on the box, an attacker finds little to use.

nodes.label: 1,500 files to 428
nodes.summary: sgit's use case ran from a tree of only the files that ran; other commands failed.

nodes.label: Compiled code did not move
nodes.summary: A 14.4 MB Rust binary, three quarters of the bytes, invisible to coverage.

nodes.label: Tests are the proof
nodes.summary: Coverage missed a compiled module; the tests caught it.

nodes.label: Files are a coarse unit
nodes.summary: 38% of statements in kept files ran; function-level removal goes further.

nodes.label: A graph from story to build
nodes.summary: Fractal semantic graphs make the minimum a walk and every file's reason a path.

nodes.label: Runtime minimisation exists
nodes.summary: SlimToolkit and RapidFort watch what a container touches and remove the rest.

nodes.label: Certify what is left
nodes.summary: Absent vulnerable code needs no patch; a traced build can be certified.

quotes.text: The evidence for what is needed is the test suite passing, not the coverage report.
a vulnerability in removed code is not a patch to apply; it is a line in the record saying the code is absent
